adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Colombia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: The article documents the national legal framework that a trans visitor stands under in the department of Cauca: consensual same-sex activity has been legal in Colombia since 1981; Congress passed a national ban on discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation in 2011; and in April 2016 the Constitutional Court legalised same-sex marriage, with the country's first same-sex wedding taking place in Cali on 24 May 2016. It also records that legal gender change has been possible since 1993 and that birth certificates offer markers F, M, NB and T. No Cauca-specific statute or incident appears in the article, so the department is assessed at this national floor.

LGBTQ rights in Colombia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: The article records a Huila-specific outcome: in ruling T-268 of 2000 the Constitutional Court permitted a gay pride parade in Neiva, the department's capital, after the Mayor of Neiva had previously prevented it - establishing constitutional protection for public expression of sexual orientation in Huila. It also documents the national floor standing over the department: same-sex activity legal since 1981, orientation-based discrimination banned since 2011, same-sex marriage legal since April 2016, and legal gender change available since 1993 with birth-certificate markers F, M, NB and T. Nothing in the article marks Huila as diverging from that national framework.
